source.scope: Source-aligned arguments for incomplete and consistent_unprovable. The first expands the self-substitution proof. The second expands the generic provability argument and its arithmetic instantiation.

nodes.name: Code refutation after substitution
nodes.lean:
let D : ℕ → Prop := fun φ : ℕ ↦
    IsSemiformula ℒₒᵣ 1 φ ∧ T.Provable (neg ℒₒᵣ <| subst ℒₒᵣ ?[numeral φ] φ)
  have D_re : REPred D := by
    have : 𝚺₁-Predicate fun φ : ℕ ↦
        IsSemiformula ℒₒᵣ 1 φ ∧ T.Provable (neg ℒₒᵣ <| subst ℒₒᵣ ?[numeral φ] φ) := by
      definability
    exact re_iff_sigma1.mpr this
  have D_spec (φ : Semisentence ℒₒᵣ 1) : D ⌜φ⌝ ↔ T ⊢ ∼φ/[⌜φ⌝] := by
    simp [D, ←provable_iff_provable, Sentence.quote_def,
      Rewriting.emb_subst_eq_subst_coe₁, Semiformula.quote_def]

nodes.name: Show D is recursively enumerable
nodes.lean:
have D_re : REPred D := by
    have : 𝚺₁-Predicate fun φ : ℕ ↦
        IsSemiformula ℒₒᵣ 1 φ ∧ T.Provable (neg ℒₒᵣ <| subst ℒₒᵣ ?[numeral φ] φ) := by
      definability
    exact re_iff_sigma1.mpr this

nodes.name: Represent D by a formula
nodes.lean:
let δ : Semisentence ℒₒᵣ 1 := codeOfREPred D
  have (n : ℕ) : D n ↔ T ⊢ δ/[↑n] := by
    simpa [Semiformula.coe_subst_eq_subst_coe₁] using re_complete D_re

nodes.name: Substitute δ’s own code
nodes.lean:
let π : Sentence ℒₒᵣ := δ/[⌜δ⌝]
  have : T ⊢ π ↔ T ⊢ ∼π := calc
    T ⊢ π ↔ T ⊢ δ/[⌜δ⌝]  := by rfl
    _     ↔ D ⌜δ⌝        := by simpa using (this ⌜δ⌝).symm
    _     ↔ T ⊢ ∼δ/[⌜δ⌝] := D_spec δ
    _     ↔ T ⊢ ∼π       := by rfl

nodes.name: Rule out both derivations
nodes.lean:
refine incomplete_def.mpr ⟨π, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro h
    exact not_consistent_iff_inconsistent.mpr
      (inconsistent_of_provable_of_unprovable h (this.mp h)) inferInstance
  · intro h
    exact not_consistent_iff_inconsistent.mpr
      (inconsistent_of_provable_of_unprovable (this.mpr h) h) inferInstance

nodes.name: Form standard provability
nodes.lean:
/-- The derivability condition D1. -/
theorem provable_D1 {σ} : T ⊢ σ → 𝗜𝚺₁ ⊢ □σ := fun h ↦
  provable_of_models _ _ fun (V : Type) _ _ ↦ by simpa [models_iff] using internalize_provability (V := V) h

/-- The derivability condition D2. -/
theorem provable_D2 {σ π} : 𝗜𝚺₁ ⊢ □(σ ➝ π) ➝ □σ ➝ □π :=
  provable_of_models _ _ fun (V : Type) _ _ ↦ by simpa [models_iff] using modus_ponens_sentence T

variable (T)

noncomputable abbrev _root_.LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvability : Provability 𝗜𝚺₁ T where
  prov := T.provable
  D1 := provable_D1

variable {T}

instance : T.standardProvability.HBL2 := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ provable_D2⟩

lemma standardProvability_def (σ : Sentence L) : T.standardProvability σ = T.provabilityPred σ := rfl

instance [T.Δ₁] : T.standardProvability.SoundOnModel ℕ :=
  ⟨fun {σ} ↦ by simp [Arithmetic.standardProvability_def, models_iff]⟩

nodes.name: Supply derivability conditions
nodes.lean:
simpa [models_iff] using Bootstrapping.Arithmetic.sigma_one_complete (T := T) (V := V) hσ

/-- The derivability condition D3. -/
theorem provable_D3 [𝗣𝗔⁻ ⪯ T] {σ : Sentence ℒₒᵣ} :
    𝗜𝚺₁ ⊢ □σ ➝ □□σ := provable_sigma_one_complete (by simp)

open LO.Entailment LO.Entailment.FiniteContext

variable {U : ArithmeticTheory}

lemma provable_D2_context [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ U] {Γ σ π} (hσπ : Γ ⊢[U] □(σ ➝ π)) (hσ : Γ ⊢[U] □σ) :
    Γ ⊢[U] □π := FiniteContext.of'! (weakening inferInstance provable_D2) ⨀! hσπ ⨀! hσ

lemma provable_D3_context [𝗣𝗔⁻ ⪯ T] [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ U] {Γ σ} (hσπ : Γ ⊢[U] □σ) :
  Γ ⊢[U] □□σ := FiniteContext.of'! (weakening inferInstance provable_D3) ⨀! hσπ

lemma provable_sound [U.SoundOnHierarchy 𝚺 1] {σ} : U ⊢ □σ → T ⊢ σ := fun h ↦ by
  have : ℕ ⊧ₘ T.provabilityPred σ := ArithmeticTheory.SoundOn.sound (F := Arithmetic.Hierarchy 𝚺 1) h (by simp)
  simpa [models_iff] using this

lemma provable_complete [U.SoundOnHierarchy 𝚺 1] [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ U] {σ} : T ⊢ σ ↔ U ⊢ □σ :=
  ⟨fun h ↦ weakening inferInstance (provable_D1 h), provable_sound⟩

instance [𝗣𝗔⁻ ⪯ T] : T.standardProvability.HBL3 := ⟨fun _ ↦ provable_D3⟩

instance [𝗣𝗔⁻ ⪯ T] : T.standardProvability.HBL where

@[simp] lemma consistent.defined : Semiformula.Evalbm V ![] (T.consistent : Sentence ℒₒᵣ) ↔ T.Consistent V := by

nodes.name: Diagonalize the provability predicate
Rule out a proof of G
nodes.lean:
variable [L.DecidableEq] [L.ReferenceableBy L] {T₀ T : Theory L} [T₀ ⪯ T] [Diagonalization T₀] [Consistent T]

variable (𝔅 : Provability T₀ T)

local notation "𝗚" => 𝔅.gödel

theorem unprovable_gödel : T ⊬ 𝗚 := by
  intro h;
  have h₁ : T ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 := D1_shift h
  have : T ⊢ ⊥ := by cl_prover [h₁, 𝔅.gödel_spec, h]
  have : ¬Consistent T := not_consistent_iff_inconsistent.mpr <|
    inconsistent_iff_provable_bot.mpr this
  contradiction

nodes.name: Formalize the implication
nodes.lean:
/-- Formalized First Incompleteness Theorem -/
theorem formalized_unprovable_gödel : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅.con ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 := by
  suffices T₀ ⊢ ∼𝔅 ⊥ ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 from this
  have h₁ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚) := 𝔅.D3 𝗚
  have h₂ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚 ➝ ⊥) := prov_distribute_imply <| by cl_prover [𝔅.gödel_spec]
  have h₃ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚 ➝ ⊥) ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚) ➝ 𝔅 ⊥ := 𝔅.D2 (𝔅 𝗚) ⊥
  cl_prover [h₁, h₂, h₃]

nodes.name: Relate G to consistency
nodes.lean:
lemma formalized_consistent_of_existance_unprovable (σ) : T₀ ⊢ ∼𝔅 σ ➝ 𝔅.con := contra! $ 𝔅.D2 _ _ ⨀ (𝔅.D1 efq!)

variable [T₀ ⪯ T] [Diagonalization T₀] (𝔅)

local notation "𝗚" => 𝔅.gödel

/-- Formalized First Incompleteness Theorem -/
theorem formalized_unprovable_gödel : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅.con ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 := by
  suffices T₀ ⊢ ∼𝔅 ⊥ ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 from this
  have h₁ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚) := 𝔅.D3 𝗚
  have h₂ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚 ➝ ⊥) := prov_distribute_imply <| by cl_prover [𝔅.gödel_spec]
  have h₃ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚 ➝ ⊥) ➝ 𝔅 (𝔅 𝗚) ➝ 𝔅 ⊥ := 𝔅.D2 (𝔅 𝗚) ⊥
  cl_prover [h₁, h₂, h₃]

theorem gödel_iff_con : T₀ ⊢ 𝗚 ⭤ 𝔅.con := by
  have h₁ : T₀ ⊢ ∼𝔅 𝗚 ➝ 𝔅.con := formalized_consistent_of_existance_unprovable 𝗚
  have h₂ : T₀ ⊢ 𝔅.con ➝ ∼𝔅 𝗚 := 𝔅.formalized_unprovable_gödel
  have h₃ : T₀ ⊢ 𝗚 ⭤ ∼𝔅 𝗚 := 𝔅.gödel_spec
  cl_prover [h₁, h₂, h₃]

nodes.name: Reduce a proof of consistency to G
nodes.lean:
theorem con_unprovable [Consistent T] : T ⊬ 𝔅.con := by
  intro h
  have : T₀ ⊢ 𝗚 ⭤ 𝔅.con := 𝔅.gödel_iff_con
  have : T ⊢ 𝗚 := by cl_prover [h, this]
  exact 𝔅.unprovable_gödel this

title: Gödel’s First and Second Incompleteness Theorems

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.incomplete.title: First incompleteness for Σ₁-sound arithmetic
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.incomplete.summary: A Δ₁-presented arithmetic theory extending R₀ and sound for Σ₁ sentences has an undecided sentence. The proof constructs a particular sentence π for which a proof of either π or its negation would give a proof of the other, contradicting consistency.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.incomplete.why_here: The local undecided sentence supplies the witness for incompleteness.

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.consistent.title: Unprovability of arithmetic consistency
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.consistent.summary: In the supplied arithmetic setting, a consistent theory T cannot prove its standard arithmetical consistency sentence. The proof applies the generic unprovability theorem to T’s standard provability predicate.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.consistent.statement_latex: \text{For the arithmetic theory }T\text{ in the supplied setting},\quad \mathrm{Consistent}(T)\Longrightarrow T\nvdash\operatorname{Con}(T),\qquad \operatorname{Con}(T)=\neg\operatorname{Prov}_T(\ulcorner\bot\urcorner)
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.consistent.why_here: This is the arithmetic specialization of the generic conclusion.

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_iff_sig.title: Recursive enumerability and Σ₁ definability
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_iff_sig.summary: The direction used here converts a Σ₁ definition of a numerical predicate into recursive enumerability.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_iff_sig.why_here: The enumerability step applies this direction to D.

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_complet.title: Provability representation of enumerable predicates
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_complet.summary: In the supplied application, an enumerable numerical predicate is represented by a formula whose numeral instance is provable in T exactly when the predicate holds of that number.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.re_complet.why_here: It supplies the representation of D under the R₀ base assumption.

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvab.title: Standard arithmetical provability
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvab.summary: This definition packages T’s arithmetized proof predicate with the rule sending an actual T-proof of σ to an IΣ₁-proof of the corresponding provability sentence.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.standardProvab.why_here: Its construction is unfolded to identify the arithmetic provability structure.

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.consistent.title: Arithmetical consistency sentence
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.consistent.summary: The standard Π₁ consistency sentence for T says that the arithmetized proof predicate does not hold of the code of contradiction.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Theory.consistent.why_here: The consistency-sentence step unfolds this definition.

lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.provable_D.title: Positive introspection in arithmetic
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.provable_D.summary: Under the supplied hypothesis PA⁻ ≼ T, IΣ₁ proves that if σ is T-provable, then the sentence asserting its T-provability is itself T-provable.
lean:LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic.provable_D.why_here: This is the D3 component described in the derivability step.

lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.göd.title: Generic Gödel fixed-point equation
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.göd.summary: With sentence coding and diagonalization available, the base theory T₀ proves that the Gödel sentence G is equivalent to the sentence denying its provability according to the chosen predicate.
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.göd.why_here: The diagonalization step summarizes the argument establishing this specification.

lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.con.title: Generic consistency unprovability
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.con.summary: Under the generic provability hypotheses, external consistency of T rules out a T-proof of the consistency sentence associated with the chosen provability predicate.
lean:LO.ProvabilityLogic.Provability.con.why_here: The generic proof step summarizes this theorem, which the arithmetic root invokes.

fact:presentation.title: Δ₁ presentation of T
fact:presentation.summary: The presentation of T’s axioms is Δ₁, supporting the arithmetization of proofs from T.
fact:presentation.why_here: It is supplied to the construction on the first branch and to the standard provability setup on the second.

fact:r0.title: T extends R₀
fact:r0.summary: The first theorem assumes that T extends the weak arithmetic base R₀.
fact:r0.why_here: This is the arithmetic base hypothesis used to represent D by provability in T.

fact:soundness.title: Σ₁ soundness of T
fact:soundness.summary: Each Σ₁ sentence proved by T is true in the standard natural numbers. In particular, this rules out a proof of contradiction.
fact:soundness.why_here: It supplies the consistency needed when either putative proof of the diagonal sentence would force a contradiction.

fact:isigma.title: Arithmetic base IΣ₁
fact:isigma.summary: IΣ₁ is the arithmetic base for the standard provability construction. The generic argument uses T₀ for the theory in which the fixed-point equation and internal implications are proved.
fact:isigma.why_here: The graph supplies this base to the standard provability, derivability, and fixed-point steps.

fact:consistency.title: Consistency of T as a hypothesis
fact:consistency.summary: The external assumption says that there is no T-proof of contradiction.
fact:consistency.why_here: It contradicts the proof of ⊥ obtained from a hypothetical T-proof of G.

step:define-D.title: Encode refutation after self-substitution
step:define-D.summary: Use the proof predicate for the presented theory T to define D(n) by two requirements. The number n must code a one-variable arithmetic formula, and T must prove the negation of the sentence obtained by substituting the numeral for n into that formula. For a genuine formula φ, the first requirement holds automatically at its code, leaving exactly the refutability test for φ at its own code.
step:define-D.why_here: It sets up the test that the proof will represent and then apply to the representing formula itself.

fact:define-D.title: The numerical predicate D
fact:define-D.summary: For a one-variable formula φ, D holds of its code exactly when T proves the negation of φ instantiated with the numeral for that code.
fact:define-D.why_here: The definition is used both to establish enumerability and to read off the refutation test at the diagonal input.

step:enumerate-D.title: Obtain recursive enumerability
step:enumerate-D.summary: Start with the coded syntax and provability tests defining D. The supplied argument gives their combined test a Σ₁ definition, so the Σ₁-to-enumerable direction of the characterization shows that D is recursively enumerable.
step:enumerate-D.why_here: Enumerability is the hypothesis needed to obtain a representing formula.

fact:enumerate-D.title: D is recursively enumerable
fact:enumerate-D.summary: There is an effective enumeration of the codes passing D’s refutation test.
fact:enumerate-D.why_here: This is the enumerability input to the representation step.

step:represent-D.title: Represent D through provability
step:represent-D.summary: Apply the representation theorem to the recursively enumerable predicate D in the setting R₀ ≼ T. It supplies a one-variable formula δ such that, for every number n, D(n) holds exactly when T proves the sentence obtained by inserting the numeral for n into δ.
step:represent-D.why_here: The representation holds for every n, including the code of δ itself.

fact:represent-D.title: Numeral-by-numeral representation
fact:represent-D.summary: The chosen formula δ represents D through an external equivalence between D(n) and the existence of a T-proof of δ at the numeral for n.
fact:represent-D.why_here: The equivalence can be instantiated at the code of the chosen δ.

step:self-substitute.title: Apply the representation to δ’s code
step:self-substitute.summary: Put the numeral for δ’s code into δ to form the sentence π. The representation equates T-provability of π with D at that code, while the defining property of D equates the same test with T-provability of ¬π. Composing these gives an equivalence between the two external proof-existence claims.
step:self-substitute.why_here: This is the point where the general representation becomes a statement about one particular sentence.

fact:self-substitute.title: Proofs of π and ¬π imply each other
fact:self-substitute.summary: For the particular diagonal instance π, existence of a T-proof of π is equivalent to existence of a T-proof of ¬π.
fact:self-substitute.why_here: Either hypothetical derivation now gives a contradictory pair of derivations.

step:exclude-both.title: Exclude both proofs by consistency
step:exclude-both.summary: Take the equivalence between proofs of π and proofs of ¬π and the consistency furnished by Σ₁ soundness. A proof on either side yields a proof on the other side, and together they yield contradiction. Hence π is an undecided sentence witnessing incompleteness.
step:exclude-both.why_here: It turns the diagonal equivalence into the two failures of provability required for the first theorem.

fact:exclude-both.title: The local undecided sentence π
fact:exclude-both.summary: The specific sentence π constructed from δ has neither a proof nor a refutation in T.
fact:exclude-both.why_here: It provides the concrete witness packaged by the theorem as incompleteness.

step:standard-provability.title: Package the standard proof predicate
step:standard-provability.summary: Start from T’s arithmetized proof predicate and write □σ for the arithmetic sentence saying that σ has a T-proof. D1 turns an actual T-proof of σ into an IΣ₁-proof of □σ. The supplied construction also verifies D2 in IΣ₁ by formalizing the combination of a proof of an implication with a proof of its antecedent.
step:standard-provability.why_here: This supplies the arithmetic provability structure used to instantiate the generic argument.

fact:standard-provability.title: Standard predicate for T-proofs
fact:standard-provability.summary: The chosen provability structure uses T’s own arithmetized proof predicate, with IΣ₁ as the base for its derivability rules.
fact:standard-provability.why_here: It supplies the predicate for the derivability conditions, the consistency sentence, and the fixed-point construction.

step:hbl-conditions.title: Complete the derivability conditions
step:hbl-conditions.summary: The arithmetic construction already supplies internalization of proofs and formalized modus ponens. Since □σ is Σ₁, the supplied formalized Σ₁-completeness result gives D3 under the stated PA⁻ base hypothesis on T, so IΣ₁ proves □σ → □□σ. This completes the Hilbert–Bernays–Löb conditions for the standard predicate.
step:hbl-conditions.why_here: The internal unprovability argument needs to combine proofs inside the predicate and to iterate the predicate.

fact:hbl-conditions.title: Hilbert–Bernays–Löb conditions
fact:hbl-conditions.summary: The standard structure supports internalization of actual proofs, formalized modus ponens, and formalized iteration of provability.
fact:hbl-conditions.why_here: These rules let the base theory reason about what a purported proof of G would entail.

step:consistency-sentence.title: Express consistency as an arithmetic sentence
step:consistency-sentence.summary: Apply T’s proof predicate to the code of contradiction and negate the resulting sentence. This produces a Π₁ sentence whose evaluation in a model expresses the absence of a T-proof of contradiction according to that model.
step:consistency-sentence.why_here: This identifies the arithmetic sentence to which the generic consistency-unprovability theorem is applied.

fact:consistency-sentence.title: The internal sentence Con(T)
fact:consistency-sentence.summary: Con(T) is the arithmetic sentence denying provability of contradiction under the standard predicate for T.
fact:consistency-sentence.why_here: It is the antecedent of the formalized implication denying provability of G.

step:godel-sentence.title: Take a fixed point of nonprovability
step:godel-sentence.summary: Apply diagonalization in the base theory T₀ to the one-variable formula that denies membership in the chosen proof predicate. It supplies a sentence G such that T₀ proves G equivalent to the result of applying that formula to G’s own code. The arithmetic specialization takes IΣ₁ as the base and uses the standard predicate for T.
step:godel-sentence.why_here: The resulting equation supplies the self-reference used in both the external and internal arguments about G.

fact:godel-sentence.title: The local Gödel fixed point
fact:godel-sentence.summary: For the chosen predicate and its fixed point G, the base theory proves an equivalence between G and the sentence asserting that G has no proof under that predicate.
fact:godel-sentence.why_here: The equation is used to rule out a proof of G, derive an internal implication, and identify G with consistency.

step:godel-unprovable.title: Derive contradiction from a proof of G
step:godel-unprovable.summary: Suppose T proves G. D1 gives a proof of □G in the base, hence also in T, and the fixed-point equation transferred from the base gives a T-proof of ¬□G from G. Thus T would prove contradiction, which external consistency rules out.
step:godel-unprovable.why_here: It establishes the external impossibility used to reject a hypothetical proof of consistency.

fact:godel-unprovable.title: No T-proof of G
fact:godel-unprovable.summary: Under external consistency and the generic base theory hypotheses, the chosen G has no proof in T.
fact:godel-unprovable.why_here: It is the external conclusion against which the final reduction argues.

step:internal-unprovability.title: Formalize why a proof of G yields contradiction
step:internal-unprovability.summary: Inside T₀, D3 turns □G into □□G. The fixed-point equation and the provability rules also turn □G into □(□G → ⊥), and D2 combines these two boxed claims to yield □⊥. Contraposition inside T₀ then yields Con(T) → ¬□G, with Con(T) interpreted through the chosen predicate.
step:internal-unprovability.why_here: This proves one direction of the internal relationship between consistency and the Gödel sentence.

fact:internal-unprovability.title: Consistency implies unprovability internally
fact:internal-unprovability.summary: The base theory proves that the internal consistency sentence implies the sentence denying provability of G.
fact:internal-unprovability.why_here: This is the forward implication from consistency needed to obtain the equivalence with G.

step:equate-godel-consistency.title: Prove G equivalent to consistency
step:equate-godel-consistency.summary: Within T₀, D1 and D2 formalize the fact that a proof of contradiction would give a proof of G, using the theorem ⊥ → G. Contraposition gives ¬□G → ¬□⊥. The internal unprovability implication gives the reverse direction, and the fixed-point equation identifies ¬□G with G, yielding the desired equivalence in T₀.
step:equate-godel-consistency.why_here: The equivalence allows an assumed proof of consistency to be used as a proof of G in any T extending the base.

fact:equate-godel-consistency.title: G and consistency are equivalent in T₀
fact:equate-godel-consistency.summary: The base theory proves that G is equivalent to the consistency sentence for the chosen provability predicate.
fact:equate-godel-consistency.why_here: This supplies the implication from the consistency sentence to G for the generic unprovability step.

step:generic-unprovability.title: Reduce a consistency proof to a proof of G
step:generic-unprovability.summary: Assume that T proves the consistency sentence for the chosen predicate. Since T extends T₀, it can use T₀’s proved implication from that sentence to G and derive G. This contradicts the external result that T has no proof of G.
step:generic-unprovability.why_here: It establishes the generic conclusion that the arithmetic theorem specializes.

fact:generic-unprovability.title: Generic failure of consistency provability
fact:generic-unprovability.summary: A consistent T satisfying the generic hypotheses has no proof of the consistency sentence associated with the chosen provability structure.
fact:generic-unprovability.why_here: Choosing the standard arithmetic provability structure yields the second root.

concepts.title: Representability of enumerable predicates
concepts.summary: A recursively enumerable numerical predicate can be represented here by an arithmetic formula whose numeral instances are provable exactly at the numbers satisfying the predicate.

concepts.title: Substitution of a formula’s own code
concepts.summary: A formula with one free input can be turned into a sentence by inserting the numeral for its own syntactic code. This allows a general test on codes to be applied to the formula representing the test.

concepts.title: Diagonal fixed points
concepts.summary: Diagonalization applied to a formula A(x) produces a sentence G such that the base theory proves G equivalent to A applied to the numeral for G’s code.

concepts.title: Arithmetized and external provability
concepts.summary: The notation T ⊢ σ asserts externally that a T-proof exists. The expression □σ is a sentence in arithmetic that asserts provability via a predicate on the code of σ and can itself occur in a theorem or inside another box.

concepts.title: Hilbert–Bernays–Löb derivability conditions
concepts.summary: D1 internalizes actual proofs, D2 formalizes modus ponens for provability claims, and D3 formalizes the passage from □σ to □□σ.

concepts.title: Consistency and its arithmetic expression
concepts.summary: External consistency says that no proof of contradiction exists in T. Its standard arithmetic expression is the sentence ¬□⊥, which a theory may reason about using its proof predicate.
